title: Tuesday's big stock stories: What’s likely to move the market in the next trading session
raw_text: Stocks @ Night is a daily newsletter delivered after hours, giving you a first look at tomorrow and last look at today. Sign up for free to receive it directly in your inbox. Here's what CNBC TV's producers were watching as the Dow Industrials dropped more than 550 points, and what's on the radar for the next session. Big reports on 'Squawk Box' Pfizer has lost 1.8% in the past three months. The stock is down 8.5% from the April high. DuPont has dropped 5% over the past three months. Shares are off 14% from the February high. PayPal has gained about 23% in the past three months, but shares are down 36% from the July 2025 high. PYPL 3M mountain Shares of PayPal in the past three months AMD reports after the bell CNBC TV's Kristina Partsinevelos will report on the chipmaker's earnings release and have instant stock, analyst and investor reaction in the 4 p.m. ET hour. In the last three months, the stock has gained 70%. In a month, it has jumped 57%. The stock hit a record on Friday, and has dropped 6% from that level. Stats from the options experts at the Cboe in Chicago show implied volatility on the stock at about 8%. That means AMD could move big either way after Tuesday afternoon's report. Frontier Airlines CNBC TV's Phil LeBeau will have earnings data from the airline. Frontier operates in more than 100 cities in the U.S., Mexico, Caribbean and Central America. It'll be a good test of how this part of the industry is operating after Spirit Airlines shut down over the weekend. ULCC is Frontier's stock ticker. The stock is in the $4 a share range. It has gained 13% in a month and nearly 22% in a year. ULCC 1Y mountain Frontier Group shares in the past 12 months South Korea The Asian nation's stock market hit another new high on Monday. The iShares MSCI South Korea ETF (EWY) tracks South Korea's booming stock market. It has surged 33% in a month and 183% in a year. No other big overseas market is even close to those numbers.
